the_fool.verse: Every grand old trip needs a beginning, darling, even when the rails run right out of track. When the smoke settles where your ride meets the mud, look in the wet grass for a little silver song.
the_fool.hint: A small silver whistle lies in the muddy grass beside the wrecked train once the danger there has passed.

the_magician.verse: You have all the tricks you need, sweet thing, you just need a wand to point them. When the painted jester takes his final bow at the village fair, check the wooden hands of his quiet little puppet.
the_magician.hint: A jester's spellcasting rod rests in the wooden hands of a lifeless marionette after the master of the village festival falls.

the_high_priestess.verse: Some secrets keep behind curtains, darling, and some hide behind porcelain. Cross the moonlit water to the island of the sick, and look upon the private shrine of the weeping lady who keeps the keys.
the_high_priestess.hint: A porcelain mask with violet filigree waits on a shrine in the private rooms of the weeping widow who rules the island sanatorium.

the_empress.verse: Mother knows best, they say, even when her house is bent as a hairpin and crawling with tails. Once the sisters and their joined beast are done cooking, darling, their big iron pot is yours for the taking.
the_empress.hint: A witch's cauldron sits in the ruins of a crooked house after the coven's fused beast is defeated.

the_emperor.verse: A boss loves his throne, honey, even if it sits in a flooded parlor where the dice never stop. Beat the grinning house at the sunken crossroads, and pry the loud iron right out of the dealer's fingers.
the_emperor.hint: A heavy blunderbuss can be taken from the dead hands of the gambler-devil who runs the casino at the drowned crossroads.

the_hierophant.verse: Old rules and red robes, darling, and a choir that howls at the crone in the sky. Climb to the high abbey in the crags, and when the head preacher's sermon is done, check his red altar.
the_hierophant.hint: A sword rests upon the cathedral altar of the red monastery in the crags after its abbot falls.

the_lovers.verse: A choice made with the heart, darling, that is the whole game, isn't it? The card points to a green tavern in the village when the night is nearly over, and something of mine waiting there. How odd.
the_lovers.hint: The clairvoyant lady's own planchette necklace waits inside the green inn at the village near the very end of the road.

the_chariot.verse: Nothing stops a driver with the reins in his teeth, sweet thing, not even a field of tall gold rows. Cut down the straw king who rules the harvest, and take the curved blade from his stuffing.
the_chariot.hint: A reaper's scythe lies on the broken body of the scarecrow lord of the corn after he falls in the fields.

strength.verse: True grit is quiet, darling, it does not boast, it just bears the weight until the work is through. Look inside the stone resting house among the misty graves for the iron that turned the earth.
strength.hint: A sturdy shovel rests inside the stone sanctuary chamber at the misty cemetery.

the_hermit.verse: Sometimes a soul has to walk into the dark trees alone with only a crooked stick for company. Find the poisoned spring deep in the blighted wood, darling, the old walker left his staff in the dirt.
the_hermit.hint: A wooden staff lies on the ground beside a befouled wellspring deep within the blighted forest.

wheel_of_fortune.verse: Up one minute, sunk the next, that is the spin of the wheel for you, jazzy as a roulette table. Wade into the dark swamp water where the roads drown, and fish up a sailor's lucky steel.
wheel_of_fortune.hint: A curved cutlass lies lost beneath the swamp water at the drowned crossroads.

justice.verse: Justice, darling, means a fair shake and an even scale for a brave soul like you. Look high in the howling peaks where red-robed monks keep their horses, and you will find a stout bit of armor hanging by the hay.
justice.hint: A knight's old shield hangs in the stables of a red-robed monastery high in the howling mountain peaks.

the_hanged_man.verse: The Hanged Man says to turn your world upside down and wait a spell, sugar. Down under the turning sails by the willow trees, a swell little music maker is waiting in the cellar dark just for you.
the_hanged_man.hint: An old banjo rests in the cellar beneath the turning sails of a village windmill among the willows.

death.verse: Oh, Death never means what it sounds like, darling, it just means an old season is over and done! Once the great sickly creature in the blighted woods takes her last bow, look up in her lair for a strange little carving.
death.hint: A carved idol hangs inside the lair of the great beast of the blighted forest, ready to be taken after she falls.

temperance.verse: Temperance is all about mixing bitter and sweet until the medicine goes down easy, doll. Up where the troubled souls rest their heads, a weeping lady in black wears a lacy little number you can claim once her tears are dried for good.
temperance.hint: A mourning veil can be lifted from the weeping widow of the hilltop sanatorium after she is laid low.

the_devil.verse: The Devil is a sly reminder of the chains we choose to wear, darling. Deep in an ancient earthen mound under the oldest trees lies a silver-topped walking stick just like Philly's, though I cannot imagine how it got there before your final test.
the_devil.hint: A gentleman's walking stick with a silver goat skull rests inside an earthen barrow deep in the oldest wood before the final trial.

the_tower.verse: The Tower means something tall and proud is coming down with a bang, sweetie! Out on the windy moors, when the giant of woven twigs tumbles into ash, look among his fallen flock for a wooden face with long ears.
the_tower.hint: A wooden mask with long hare ears can be taken from a fallen zealot on the moors after the great wicker figure burns.

the_star.verse: The Star is pure hope shining in the dark, darling, and it brings you a swell present rather than a dusty trinket. Topple the many-legged old crone skittering deep in the mine tunnels, and you will walk out with a brand new knack.
the_star.hint: A special present, a brand new knack of your own, awaits you once the centipede hag of the deep mine tunnels falls.

the_moon.verse: The Moon is full of tricks and shadows, doll, but for you it means a present money cannot buy. Put an end to the sneaky weasel crone in her leaning, crooked house, and three lucky twists of fate will be all yours.
the_moon.hint: A special present, three lucky twists of fate, comes to you after the weasel hag of the crooked house falls.

the_sun.verse: The Sun is the bee's knees, darling, bringing warmth, truth, and a grand present just for you! Settle the hash of that cooing, feathered crone playing at delivering the mail, and a lasting gift of strength will put pep in your step.
the_sun.hint: A special present, a lasting gift of strength, arrives after you defeat the pigeon hag who poses as the village postmaster.

judgement.verse: Judgement calls the sleepers to wake up and face the music, sugar. Out in the misty boneyard, once the chained harvester drops his rattle in the shrouded tomb, you will find his bright little light sitting right on the cold stone floor.
judgement.hint: A ghostly lantern rests on the stone floor of a shrouded tomb in the misty cemetery after its chained reaper falls.

the_world.verse: The World is the last card in the deck and the first in the book, darling, the whole grand dance complete! Bring down the horned lord of the oldest wood, and the finest present of all, one true wish, belongs to you.
the_world.hint: A final present, a single wish of your choosing, is granted after the horned god of the oldest wood falls.

summaries.the_fool: A step onto the road before you know where it goes.
summaries.the_magician: Will and trickery, a hand that makes things happen.
summaries.the_high_priestess: What is known and not said; a veil and a door.
summaries.the_empress: Plenty and the hearth, mother and pot and house.
summaries.the_emperor: Order, rule and the throne that holds the table.
summaries.the_hierophant: Old rites, a creed and the one who keeps it.
summaries.the_lovers: A choice made with the heart, and what it costs.
summaries.the_chariot: Drive and victory, the reins held in the teeth.
summaries.strength: Quiet courage that bears the weight until the work is done.
summaries.the_hermit: One who walks the dark alone with a lamp or a stick.
summaries.wheel_of_fortune: Up one turn and down the next; luck's own table.
summaries.justice: A fair scale and a held line.
summaries.the_hanged_man: Surrender and a world seen upside down.
summaries.death: An old season ending so another can begin.
summaries.temperance: Bitter and sweet mixed until the medicine goes down.
summaries.the_devil: The chains we choose to wear, and the one who sells them.
summaries.the_tower: Something proud brought down with a bang and a fire.
summaries.the_star: Hope in the dark; a present, not a treasure.
summaries.the_moon: Shadows and tricks, and a present that money cannot buy.
summaries.the_sun: Warmth and plain truth, and a grand gift of strength.
summaries.judgement: The sleepers called up to face what they did.
summaries.the_world: The last card in the deck and the first in the book.
